newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Early data points to steady Philippine Q1 growth.
newsitem.headline: Early data points to steady Philippine Q1 growth.

text.p: Early economic indicators all point to a steady first quarter gross national product (GNP) growth, a senior Philippine official said on Tuesday.

Socorro Zingapan, director of the National Planning and Policy Staff of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), said although it was too early to predict the first quarter GNP growth rate, early indicators showed steady growth.
"We have a good export growth rate in the first two months of the year," she told Reuters.
Merchandise exports rose by 55 percent in the first two months of the year to $4.685 billion from $3.014 billion a year-ago.
She said the agriculture sector, which contributed substantially in last year's growth, did not suffer from drought nor heavy flooding during the period.
"There's no bad news coming out from the agriculture sector. There's no request to import," she added.
The preliminary figures are scheduled to be released by the end of next month.
Earlier, NEDA director-general Cielito Habito said he expected first quarter GNP to expand by between six to 6.5 percent.
Zingapan said the government did not scale down its full-year GNP growth projection of between seven to eight percent for this year.
Philippine GNP grew by 6.8 percent last year, the highest growth rate since 1990.
